b: Taking place in Valencia from 10–13 Nov, the Spanish trade fair introduces a new hall dedicated to industrialised construction and a programme of more than 100 conferences.
Visitors outside Feria Valencia for FIMMA + Maderalia 2026

FIMMA + Maderalia 2026 is taking place at Feria Valencia in Spain from 10–13 Nov, bringing together manufacturers and suppliers of machinery, technology, components and solutions for the furniture and woodworking industries.
The biennial event features 447 direct exhibitors and 927 represented companies and brands, 3% more than in 2024. It occupies six exhibition halls across two levels, covering more than 72,000 sq m.

“The joint organisation of FIMMA and Maderalia is one of the great strengths of this trade fair and a formula that allows us to offer the industry a unique industrial and commercial platform in Europe,” said Santi Riera, president of the FIMMA organising committee.

International exhibitors account for 43% of the total, with companies from 28 countries, including Germany, Austria, China, Italy, the US, India and Vietnam. The organisers aim to strengthen the fair’s international business links, particularly between European and Asian manufacturers and Latin American markets.
Biesse is among the machinery manufacturers exhibiting at FIMMA + Maderalia 2026

FIMMA + Maderalia has expanded its International Buyers Programme, tripling its budget to attract more than 500 buyers from strategic markets, particularly the EU, the Maghreb and Latin America. B2B meetings will connect exhibitors with international buyers, distributors, specifiers and other industry professionals.

The initiative is being organised in collaboration with ICEX, the Valencian regional government’s IVACE+i Internacional agency, and industry associations including ARVET (Spanish Association of Exporting Companies), COFEARFE (Spanish Federation of Hardware and DIY Manufacturers) and ASEMAD, the regional employers’ association for the carpentry industry in the Valencian Community.

“The Spanish wood and furniture industry has extraordinary production, technological and business capabilities, with the Valencian Community being one of its leading centres,” said Alejandro Bermejo, president of the Maderalia organising committee.
“We are a sector with an enormous capacity for adaptation, innovation and value creation, and FIMMA + Maderalia is precisely the best reflection of that strength,” he added.
Conferences will examine architecture and new industrialised construction systems

A key addition to the 2026 edition is the Industrialised Construction Hall, which will bring together about 100 companies involved in the sector, including manufacturers, architects, builders, developers and specifiers.

The programme will examine new construction systems and the use of wood, components and technology in industrialised building. Speakers will include architects Xavier Vilalta, Juan Trías de Bes and Pau Bajet, alongside specialists from the Valencian Building Institute (IVE). Other sessions will cover Passivhaus standards and initiatives by Cesefor and Club Madera.

A live timber construction project will demonstrate modular building methods. Designed by architect Dani Sirvent Pérez and built by SIDO Madera, the house will be assembled during the four-day event before being dismantled and relocated to become the architect’s permanent home.
Areas for interior design and carpentry
FIMMA + Maderalia 2026 occupies six exhibition halls across two levels of Feria Valencia
The fair will also introduce its first Interior Design and Contract Agora, organised by the College of Interior Designers of the Valencian Community (CDICV) and sponsored by Cucine Home Group.
The area will bring together professionals from interior design, decoration and the contract sector to encourage collaboration with manufacturers and suppliers.
An adjacent EASD Space will feature work by students and emerging designers, with contributions from EASD, the training centres of Catarroja and Paterna, and sponsor Lamiplast.
Technology, training and demonstrations across six halls
KDT Machinery is among the woodworking technology exhibitors
Other exhibition areas will focus on automation, innovation, training and traditional woodworking skills.

These include an industrial robotics area for housing construction by Hundegger and the Essential Innovation Showcase by AIDIMME. The latter will feature technological developments, while the Door Show will present products and solutions for the door industry.

Training and skills development will feature in the La Carpintería area, promoted by Profemadera, while Mucho + Que Carpintería will showcase content creators and industry influencers, including a podcast by Fermín Lorda.
ASEMAD’s Active Carpentry Plaza will also demonstrate the work of carpentry professionals and their role in the wider industrial supply chain.
